--- title: "panel D" --- # panel d — erin brokowich *Erin Brockovich in Hinkley, California: a hand-built plume of contaminated water and the homes of the families she met.* ### 1. See the table What is a case? Which columns are Quant / Qual? What is missing? First, a base map pointed at Hinkley, so we can check we are in the right place. `Esri.WorldImagery` is satellite, so the PG&E site, streets and houses show up at zoom 14. Tibble #1: the plume. Each row is one corner of the plume POLYGON. It starts at the PG&E tanks and runs about 1 mile southwards towards Hinkley. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plume <- tibble( lng = c(-117.2135, -117.2095, -117.2040, -117.2030, -117.2090, -117.2160, -117.2165), lat = c( 34.9460, 34.9460, 34.9380, 34.9270, 34.9230, 34.9290, 34.9390) ) plume ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 7 × 2 lng lat 1 -117. 34.9 2 -117. 34.9 3 -117. 34.9 4 -117. 34.9 5 -117. 34.9 6 -117. 34.9 7 -117. 34.9 ``` ::: ::: Tibble #2: the families. Each row (case) is one family's home, as a POINT. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} families <- tibble( family = c("Jensen", "Robinson", "Irving", "Matthews", "Gomez"), address = c("12 Mountain View Rd", "40 Acacia St", "7 Summerset Rd", "88 Community Blvd", "25 Serra Rd"), phone = c("555-0101", "555-0102", "555-0103", "555-0104", "555-0105"), people = c(4, 3, 5, 2, 6), illness = c("Breast cancer", "Tumours", "Nosebleeds", "Headaches", "Rashes"), severity = c("High", "High", "Medium", "Low", "Medium"), water_from = c("Well", "Well", "Well", "Well", "Well"), signed_up = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "No", "Yes"), col = c("red", "red", "orange", "yellow", "orange"), lng = c(-117.2100, -117.2075, -117.2120, -117.2060, -117.2135), lat = c( 34.9400, 34.9350, 34.9310, 34.9260, 34.9290) ) families ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 5 × 11 family address phone people illness severity water_from signed_up col lng 1 Jensen 12 Mou… 555-… 4 Breast… High Well Yes red -117. 2 Robins… 40 Aca… 555-… 3 Tumours High Well Yes red -117. 3 Irving 7 Summ… 555-… 5 Nosebl… Medium Well Yes oran… -117. 4 Matthe… 88 Com… 555-… 2 Headac… Low Well No yell… -117. 5 Gomez 25 Ser… 555-… 6 Rashes Medium Well Yes oran… -117. # ℹ 1 more variable: lat ``` ::: ::: My data has: - `plume`: 7 rows and 2 columns. Each row is one corner of the plume. - `families`: 5 rows and 11 columns. Each row is one family's home. - `family`, `address`, `phone`: Qualitative, categorical. Encoded . One per family. - `illness`: Qualitative, categorical. Encoded - `severity`: Qualitative, ordinal ("Low" < "Medium" < "High"). Encoded - `water_from`: Qualitative, categorical. Encoded . Every family drinks well water. - `signed_up`: Qualitative, categorical ("Yes" / "No"). Did the family join the case against PG&E? - `col`: the colour for each `severity`, used to colour the markers. - `people`: Quantitative, numeric. How many people live in the home. - `lng`, `lat`: Quantitative, numeric. Where the point is. There is no missing data. Everything is made up by hand: the families, addresses, phone numbers and illnesses are hypothetical, and the coordinates are approximate. ### 2. Ask ~~One question *this* table can answer. One it cannot. Write both.~~ Possibly can answer: 1. Which families live on top of the plume, and how sick are they? (Main Character Question) Possibly cannot answer: 1. Did the chromium in the water *cause* the illnesses? (No water tests or medical records) 2. How did the plume grow over the years? (One snapshot only) ### 3. Choose a mark 1. Interactive map (`leaflet`): plume as `addPolygons()`, homes as `addCircleMarkers()` coloured by `severity`, with popups and a legend ### 4. Predict 1. I think the families closest to the PG&E tanks, in the middle of the plume, will have the most severe illnesses. ### 5. Make **Which families live on top of the plume, and how sick are they?** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Question 1 popup <- paste( "", families$family, "
", families$address, "
", "Phone: ", families$phone, "
", "People at home: ", families$people, "
", "Illness: ", families$illness, "
", "Severity: ", families$severity, "
", "Water from: ", families$water_from, "
", "Signed up: ", families$signed_up, "
" ) leaflet(data = families) %>% addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery") %>% setView(lng = -117.2050, lat = 34.9360, zoom = 14) %>% # Tibble #1: the plume addPolygons( lng = plume$lng, lat = plume$lat, color = "purple", weight = 2, fill = TRUE, fillColor = "purple", popup = "Contaminated groundwater plume" ) %>% # The PG&E tanks addMarkers( lng = -117.2115, lat = 34.9455, label = "PG&E compressor station (tanks)", labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = TRUE, textOnly = FALSE, textsize = 14) ) %>% # Tibble #2: the families, coloured by severity addCircleMarkers( lng = ~lng, lat = ~lat, radius = 8, # Pixels color = families$col, stroke = FALSE, fillOpacity = 1, label = families$family, popup = popup ) %>% addLegend( title = "Illness severity", colors = c("red", "orange", "yellow"), labels = c("High", "Medium", "Low") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### 6. Say Every family on the map lives on top of the plume and drinks well water. The two families closest to the PG&E tanks, the Jensens and the Robinsons, have the most severe illnesses, while the Matthews family, at the far southern tip of the plume, has the mildest. ### 7. Limit - Isn't proof that the chromium caused the illnesses - Doesn't speak for the whole town (only 5 made-up families) - Isn't known how the plume spread over TIME
